sense: first, earliest, as it was at the start

evidence: Verg. A. 1.372: prīmā repetēns ab orīgine
terms.comment: Latin calls the original state of a thing its first: going back to the very beginning is prīmā repetere ab orīgine. Originally is ā prīncipiō or prīmō.

evidence: Tac. Ann. 1.1: Urbem Rōmam ā prīncipiō rēgēs habuēre

terms.gloss: original, former (of a state or condition)
evidence: Nep. Timol. 1.1: in prīstinum restituere, to restore to its original state (Lewis & Short)
Varr. LL 6.36: verba prīmigenia, original words, from which others are formed (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Rare: Varro, then late writers (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Apul. M. 11.2: Cerēs … frūgum parēns orīginālis (Lewis & Short)
Hier. in Gal. 3.10: orīginālēs librī, the books in their original language (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Late Latin (Apuleius, Jerome, Macrobius), not classical.

phrases.latin: Urbem Rōmam ā prīncipiō rēgēs habuēre
phrases.english: the city of Rome was originally ruled by kings

phrases.latin: ut nōn sōlum in prīstinum statum redīssent, sed omnium temporum dignitātem et grātiam antecessisse vidērentur
phrases.english: so that they had not only been restored to their original position, but seemed to have surpassed their standing and influence at any time before

pristinus.html: De Vaan 489, s.v. prior: from the zero grade *prīs- of the comparative, as in prīscus and prīdem.
